title: RSA run 1
summary: Six inner-loop cells on Sherlock, 7 October 2026: the combined reference-game data (5 sources, 40k training trials) twice, and two recovery conditions twice each, with a ground-truth model withheld from the seeds. 5 rounds × 6 Gemini 3.8 Flash agents per cell.
findings: Recovery works on prediction distance: in all four recovery cells the exported model is 0.004–0.009 RMSE from the withheld ground truth, against 0.048–0.049 for the best starting model, and a live model sits even closer (0.0001–0.004).
On real data the loop finds models that generalise to held-out conditions: the best are +67 to +94 lpd over rsa_l2 (2–2.6 clustered SE), almost all of it on pragmods.

Models specialise by source. Re-scored with grouped CV on the training conditions, the five sources have five different best models in each real cell, and real_rep1's exported model wins on Sikos 2021 (+263 over rsa_l2) while losing on pragmods (-38), where a literal/pragmatic mixture leads (+117). The held-out test, with few held-out conditions per source, weights pragmods heavily, so run 1's 'selection picked the wrong model' was overstated: the two measures agree source by source.
Literal/pragmatic mixtures and softmax-belief listeners are among the best held-out models in both real replicates.
decisions: Fixed before run 2 (PLAN.md, 2026-10-08): select and prune on grouped CV over training conditions; live-set cap 12 by total ELPD-CV; no source-specific rule; per-source results descriptive only.
Recovery verdict: RMSE to the ground truth <= 0.01 alone; the seeds' and the closest live model's distances reported.
Agents have no internet access (shell under a no-network filter; web tools denied).
Run 2: real data x 3 replicates x 8 rounds, recovery x 2 replicates x 4 rounds, on the mcfrank partition.
